ἔργων προφητείαν ἀλληγορίαν ὠνόμασεν. Gal 4,25 Οὐχ ἁπλῶς ἐμνημόνευσε τοῦ
Σινᾶ ὄρους, ἀλλ' ἐπειδὴ οἱ Ἀγαρηνοὶ οἱ ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἰσμαὴλ τὴν ἔρημον ἔχουσι τὴν
παρατείνουσαν ἕως τοῦ Σινᾶ ὄρους. ἐν δὲ τῷ Σινᾷ ὁ νόμος ἐδόθη εἰς δουλείαν
γεννῶν, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ Σινᾶ ὄρους αἱ πλάκες δοθεῖσαι ἐκομίσθησαν ἐν τῷ Ἰσραήλ, καὶ
πολλάκις μετενεχθεῖσαι ἀπὸ τόπου εἰς τόπον τελευταῖον ἱδρύθησαν ἐν
Ἱεροσολύμοις. διὰ τοῦτο ἐπήγαγεν· συστοιχεῖ δὲ τῇ νῦν Ἱερουσαλήμ, δουλεύει δὲ
μετὰ τῶν τέκνων αὐτῆς. ὅπου γῆς ἐπαγγελία, καὶ κτῆσις καὶ γάμος καὶ τὰ
ἀνθρώπινα, καὶ δουλεία ἀκολουθεῖ· ὅπου δὲ ἀπαλλαγὴ τῶν ἐπὶ γῆς φροντίδων καὶ
τῶν δεσμῶν, καὶ ἐν οὐρανοῖς ἡ πολιτεία, ἐξ αὐτῆς τῆς πολιτείας ἡ ἐλευθερία. Gal
5,17 Ζητεῖται διὰ τί νόμου ἀποσπῶν μέμνηται τῆς ἁμαρτίας. ἐπειδὴ τρυφᾶν ἐκέλευεν
ὁ νόμος, διὰ δὲ τούτου διερεθίζεται ἡ ἐπιθυμία καὶ ἀκατάσχετος οὖσα πρὸς ἁμαρτίαν
ἄγει. τούτου ἕνεκεν ὅτε νόμου ἦν μνήμη, μέμνηται καὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας. καὶ γὰρ ἐν τῇ
πρὸς Ῥωμαίους τοῦ νόμου μνημονεύων καὶ τῆς διὰ τοῦ κυρίου διορθώσεως
εἰσήγαγεν, τὸ οἱ γὰρ κατὰ σάρκα ζῶντες θεῷ ἀρέσαι οὐ δύνανται. διὰ τί δὲ
συνεχωρήθη τὸ τρυφᾶν καὶ ἐσθίειν; ὅτι ἡ τῶν ὡμολογημένων κακῶν ἀποχὴ οὐκ ἂν
προεχώρησεν, εἰ μὴ ἐνεδόθη αὐτοῖς τὸ ἐσθίειν 304 καὶ πίνειν· ᾔδει μὲν γὰρ ὁ
νομοθέτης ὅτι ἀδύνατον τρυφῶντας κρατεῖν ἡδονῶν. τέως δὲ ἠθέλησε τὸν νοῦν
παιδεῦσαι, ἵνα γνῷ τί καλὸν καὶ τί κακὸν καὶ τί τὸ εὐσεβές· προεώρα γὰρ ὅτι ἔμελλεν
ἔρχεσθαι ὁ τὸ λεῖπον τῷ νόμῳ προστιθείς, λέγω δὴ τὸ μὴ κατὰ σάρκα περιπατεῖν, ὡς
λέγει ὁ Παῦλος. Gal 6,7–8 Ἐδήλωσεν ἐκ τούτου ὅτι πολλοὶ ἀκαίρως μὲν ἀνήλισκον,
παρέχοντες τοῖς τηρεῖν νόμον παρακελευομένοις, τοῖς δὲ τὴν Παύλου διδασκαλίαν
κηρύττουσιν οὐδὲν παρεῖχον. διό φησιν· ὁ σπείρων εἰς τὴν σάρκα αὐτοῦ· ὁ γὰρ νόμῳ
ὑποκείμενος ἐν τοῖς σαρκικοῖς ζῇ. ὁ τοίνυν τῷ ταῦτα διδάσκοντι παρέχων εἰς τὴν
σάρκα σπείρει μόνον. Gal 6,14–15 Ἵνα μὴ νομισθῇ ἀκροβυστίας ἀντιποιεῖσθαι, καὶ
οὐχὶ περιτομῆς καὶ διαβολῆς πρόφασιν δῷ τοῖς ἀντιλέγουσιν, κάλλιστα ἐπήγαγε τὸ
τελευταῖον, ὅτι οὔτε περιτομή τι ἰσχύει οὔτε ἀκροβυστία, καινὴν δὲ κτίσιν εἶπεν.
περὶ ἧς ἀλλαχοῦ· εἴ τις ἐν Χριστῷ, καινὴ κτίσις. εἰ καινή, φησί, κτίσις, μὴ γίνου ὑπὸ
νόμον· ὁ γὰρ ζῶν κατὰ νόμον ἐν κόσμῳ ζῇ, ὁ δὲ ζῶν ἐν Χριστῷ, ἐν οὐρανοῖς
πολιτεύεται. ἐσταύρωται οὖν ἐμοὶ κόσμος κἀγὼ κόσμῳ.
thought_title: Sinai slavery, indulgence under law, and new creation
orientation: Severianus is closing his comments on Galatians, explaining Sinai and Jerusalem, law and desire, and circumcision and new creation.
pass_a_gloss: Now therefore he called the prophecy through works allegory. He mentioned Mount Sinai not simply, but because the Hagarites, those from Ishmael, hold the desert, the one extending as far as Mount Sinai. In Sinai the law was given, begetting into slavery, and from Mount Sinai the tablets when given were carried into Israel, and often transferred from place to place at last were established in Jerusalem. For this reason he added: but she corresponds to the present Jerusalem, and she is enslaved with her children. Where there is promise of land, and possession and marriage and human things, slavery also follows; but where there is release from the cares upon earth and from bonds, and citizenship is in the heavens, freedom comes from the citizenship itself. It is asked why, when pulling away from law, he mentions sin. Because the law commanded to live luxuriously, and through this desire is provoked and being uncontrollable leads to sin. For this reason when there was mention of law, he mentions sin also. For also in the letter to the Romans, when mentioning the law, he introduced also the correction through the Lord, namely for those living according to flesh are not able to please God. And why was living luxuriously and eating permitted? Because abstinence from acknowledged evils would not have advanced, unless to eat and to drink had been granted to them; for the lawgiver knew that it is impossible while living luxuriously to master pleasures. But for the meanwhile he wished to educate the mind, in order that it might know what is good and what is evil and what is pious; for he foresaw that the one adding to the law what was lacking was about to come, I mean not walking according to flesh, as Paul says. From this he showed that many were spending out of due season, yielding to those urging to keep law, but to those preaching the teaching of Paul they yielded nothing. Therefore he says: the one sowing into his own flesh; for the one subject to law lives among fleshly things. Whoever therefore yields to the one teaching these things sows only into the flesh. In order that he might not be thought to contend for uncircumcision, and give to opponents a pretext for circumcision and slander, most fittingly he added at the end that neither circumcision avails anything nor uncircumcision, but he said new creation. About which elsewhere: if anyone is in Christ, new creation. If, he says, new creation, do not become under law; for the one living according to law lives in the world, but the one living in Christ lives as citizen in the heavens. Therefore world has been crucified to me and I to world.

pass_b_english: So Paul here calls prophecy carried out through events allegory. He does not name Mount Sinai lightly. The Hagarites, who descend from Ishmael, hold the desert that stretches all the way to Mount Sinai. On Sinai the law was given, giving birth to slavery. The tablets given on Mount Sinai were carried among Israel, moved many times from place to place, and finally settled in Jerusalem. That is why Paul adds, "It corresponds to the present Jerusalem, because she is enslaved with her children" (Galatians 4:25).

Where there is a promise of land, with possession and marriage and human concerns, slavery follows. Where there is release from earthly cares and bonds, and citizenship is in heaven, freedom comes from that citizenship itself.

The question is raised why Paul, when he draws people away from the law, still mentions sin. Severianus answers that the law told people to live luxuriously, and indulgence excites desire, and when desire runs unchecked it leads to sin. So whenever the law is recalled, sin is recalled too. In the letter to the Romans Paul does the same: when he recalls the law and the correction that comes through the Lord, he brings in the words, "Those who live according to the flesh cannot please God" (Romans 8:8). But why, it is asked, were living luxuriously and eating and drinking allowed at all? Because turning away from acknowledged evils would never have advanced unless eating and drinking had been granted. The lawgiver knew that people who live luxuriously cannot master pleasure. For the time being he wanted to train the mind to know what is good and what is evil and what is holy. He foresaw the coming of the one who would supply what the law lacked—I mean no longer walking according to the flesh, as Paul says.

From this text (Galatians 6:7–8) Paul made clear that many were spending their resources unwisely. They gave to those who urged them to keep the law, and they gave nothing to those who preach Paul's teaching. So Paul says, "The one who sows to his own flesh" (Galatians 6:8). Anyone subject to the law lives among fleshly things. Whoever provides for a teacher of such things sows only to the flesh.

Finally, Paul adds something very well, so he will not seem to claim uncircumcision rather than circumcision, and so give his opponents no excuse for slander: "Neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything" (Galatians 6:15), but he spoke of a new creation. About it he says elsewhere, "If anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation" (2 Corinthians 5:17). If it is a new creation, Paul says, do not come under the law. Whoever lives according to the law lives in the world, but whoever lives in Christ exercises his citizenship in heaven. So, "The world has been crucified to me, and I to the world" (Galatians 6:14).
notes: 304 in τὸ ἐσθίειν 304 καὶ πίνειν is a printed page number, not source text; glossed as to eat and to drink

problems.quote: They yielded to those who urged them to keep the law, and they yielded nothing to those who preach Paul's teaching.
problems.source_quote: παρέχοντες τοῖς τηρεῖν νόμον παρακελευομένοις, τοῖς δὲ τὴν Παύλου διδασκαλίαν κηρύττουσιν οὐδὲν παρεῖχον.
problems.why: The verb here means giving material support or providing for teachers, not yielding or submitting to them.
problems.fix: They gave to those who urged them to keep the law, while giving nothing to those who preach Paul's teaching.

problems.quote: Whoever yields to a teacher of such things
problems.source_quote: ὁ τοίνυν τῷ ταῦτα διδάσκοντι παρέχων
problems.why: The participle means giving to or financially supporting such a teacher, not yielding to him.
problems.fix: Whoever provides for a teacher of such things

problems.quote: when he recalls the law, he also brings in the correction that comes through the Lord, "Those who live according to the flesh cannot please God"
problems.source_quote: τοῦ νόμου μνημονεύων καὶ τῆς διὰ τοῦ κυρίου διορθώσεως εἰσήγαγεν, τὸ οἱ γὰρ κατὰ σάρκα ζῶντες θεῷ ἀρέσαι οὐ δύνανται.
problems.why: The genitive 'correction through the Lord' is governed by 'mentioning,' not 'brought in'; the English wrongly equates Romans 8:8 with that correction.
problems.fix: when he recalls the law and the correction that comes through the Lord, he brings in the words, "Those who live according to the flesh cannot please God"
problems.ruling: μνημονεύων governs law and διὰ τοῦ κυρίου διορθώσεως; εἰσήγαγεν introduces the quote, not equates it with that correction.

problems.why: The subject of the verb is Paul, not Severianus; Paul made this clear in the preceding verses, leading into 'So Paul says.'
problems.ruling: Ἐδήλωσεν ἐκ τούτου with διό φησιν points to Paul’s argument in Galatians, not Severianus as subject.

problems.quote: many spent themselves at the wrong time
problems.why: The verb means spending money or resources (supporting teachers, cf. Gal 6:6-8), not exhausting oneself ('spent themselves').
problems.fix: many were spending their resources unwisely
problems.ruling: ἀνηλίσκον means spending resources, matching παρέχοντες support; not reflexive self-exhaustion.

fixed: Yielding -> giving: παρέχοντες/παρείχον means material giving to teachers (cf. Gal 6:6-8), not submitting.
Yields to a teacher -> provides for a teacher: τῷ ταῦτα διδάσκοντι παρέχων means financially supporting him.
Correction syntax: τοῦ νόμου ... καὶ τῆς ... διορθώσεως both depend on μνημονεύων; τὸ ... is what εἰσήγαγεν introduces.
Agency: subject of Ἐδήλωσεν ... διό φησιν is Paul, not Severianus.
Spent themselves -> spending resources: ἀνήλισκον means spending money/resources on teachers, not exhausting oneself.

problems.quote: From this Paul made clear that many were spending their resources unwisely.
problems.source_quote: Gal 6,7–8 Ἐδήλωσεν ἐκ τούτου ὅτι πολλοὶ ἀκαίρως μὲν ἀνήλισκον
problems.why: Severianus ties misspending to Gal 6:7–8; English "this" follows the lawgiver digression instead.
problems.fix: From Galatians 6:7–8 Paul showed that many spent unwisely, supporting law-keepers, not gospel preachers.
problems.ruling: Omitting 'Gal 6,7–8' leaves 'ἐκ τούτου' ('From this') pointing to the preceding Gal 5:17 lawgiver passage, misleading readers about the referent.

edits.old: From this Paul made clear that many were spending their resources unwisely.
edits.new: From this text (Galatians 6:7–8) Paul made clear that many were spending their resources unwisely.

fixed: omission Gal 6,7-8: fixed ἐκ τούτου ambiguity by anchoring to this text (Galatians 6:7–8)
no edit: παρέχοντες / οὐδὲν παρεῖχον mean give/provide, so 'gave' is correct
no edit: τῷ ταῦτα διδάσκοντι παρέχων means one providing for a teacher, so 'provides for' is correct

no edit: πολλοὶ ἀκαίρως μὲν ἀνήλισκον with παρέχοντες context means spending resources unwisely

last_rejected.why: The source does not name Severianus; he is the author speaking directly, and shifting to third person clashes with his first-person 'I mean' later in the paragraph.
last_rejected.ruling: Greek ἐπειδὴ gives the causal answer; no name. Adding Severianus is editorial voice, not a change to law-luxury-sin sense.
